subject: DPA negotiation: backup/DR carve-outs, subprocessors, and DocuSign
messages:
From: Elena Keller <elena.keller@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Burns <tom.burns@acme.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline + backup/DR carve-out question

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA. We've reviewed and attached a redline with two items we need clarified before our procurement counsel will sign:

1) Backup/DR carve-out — we need explicit language permitting retention of copies in encrypted backups for disaster recovery for a limited period after deletion requests. Please confirm maximum retention, controls around restore, and whether you will log any restores that involve Customer Personal Data.

2) Subprocessors & transfers — we've asked for an up-to-date subprocessor list and confirmation of legal mechanisms for EU->US transfers (SCCs or other). We have some internal compliance gates around transfers to third countries.

Attached: DPA_redline_acme_v2.docx (redlines inline) and Subprocessor_List_20260510.pdf

We are targeting signature this week if we can resolve the backup/DR language and confirm subprocessors. Can you loop in Redwood legal?

Thanks,
Elena Keller
Head of Procurement — Acme Corp.
(elena.keller@acme.com)

Elena — thanks for the redline and the detail. Looping in Aditya (legal) and Jasmine (sales ops) so we can get you a clean counter.

Quick answers up front:
- Subprocessors: the attached list is the most recent; we will confirm any planned additions.
- Transfers: Redwood uses SCCs for EU transfers by default and will provide export/config details.
- Backup/DR: I understand your ask for brief retention to support restores — we want to be explicit and narrow.

Aditya / Legal — can you review Acme's suggested language regarding "backups" and propose a tight clause we can send back? Our preference is to avoid a broadly worded carve-out but provide an explicit limited exception for encrypted backups used solely for DR with strict access controls and time limits.

Elena — if you prefer, we can propose a short paragraph to insert into Section 6 (Data Retention & Deletion) to try to close quickly. Also happy to jump on a 20-min call if that helps speed sign-off.

Next steps: Aditya to propose language today; I'll follow up with DocuSign routing once we have agreed text.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elena Keller <elena.keller@acme.com>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: DPA redline + backup/DR carve-out question

Elena / Marissa — thanks for the context. I've reviewed Acme's redline and propose the following compromise language aimed at narrow, auditable DR exceptions while addressing Acme's compliance needs:

Proposed insertion to Section 6 (Data Retention & Deletion):
"Notwithstanding deletion requests or Customer instructions to delete, Redwood may retain Customer Personal Data contained within encrypted disaster recovery backups for a period not to exceed thirty (30) calendar days solely for the purpose of restoring Customer data in the event of data loss or system failure. Such backups will be encrypted both at-rest and in-transit, access is restricted to personnel on a documented need-to-know basis, and any restoration activity that results in access to Customer Personal Data will be logged and disclosed to Customer upon request. Redwood will securely delete Customer Personal Data from backups within ninety (90) calendar days following termination of the Agreement or final deletion request, unless otherwise required by applicable law."
Notes / rationale:
- 30-day backup retention post-deletion is industry-common and limits exposure while keeping DR operationally feasible.
- 90-day maximum for deletion from backups after termination gives operations reasonable window to complete secure erasure across multiple storage tiers.
- We add the requirement for encrypted backups and restoration audit logs to meet Acme's evidence needs.

On subprocessors: Redwood will provide an updated list as of the date of signing and notify Acme of additions per the existing notice cadence. For EU->US transfers, Redwood will rely on SCCs supplemented by standard technical controls; we will provide a copy of the executed SCCs as part of the DPA exhibits.

If Acme accepts the proposed paragraph, we can incorporate it as a single tracked-change update and route the DPA for signature via DocuSign. I can also prepare an "Exhibit B — Subprocessors & Transfers" with the final subprocessor list.

Marissa — want me to send the revised DPA and a DocuSign envelope (routing to Elena + Acme signatures then Redwood exec)?

Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
